state.semantics: Process events in increasing timestamp order, not list order. Control events enable or disable the named rule immediately. Each signal can fire at most one enabled rule. A rule matches when its event_type and target match the signal (target='any' matches all), its min_value is not greater than the signal value, and its required_state is null or equals the target's current state. A rule can fire at timestamp t only if it has never fired or t - last_fired >= cooldown. Choose the eligible rule with greatest priority, breaking ties by smaller numeric rule ID. Firing sets the target's boolean state to the rule's set_state value; it also updates last_fired even when the value was already satisfied. A control event never fires a rule.

A rule can fire at timestamp t only if it has never fired or t - last_fired >= cooldown. Choose the eligible rule with greatest priority, breaking ties by smaller numeric rule ID. Firing sets the target's boolean state to the rule's set_state value; it also updates last_fired even when the value was already satisfied. A control event never fires a rule.

When multiple cheapest routes exist, choose the lexicographically smallest first hop. An edge is essential when closing that edge would make the cheapest valid route more expensive or unreachable.
